youtube.title: Count to a billion | Possibility Lab No. 004
youtube.caption:
Can you count to a billion? Out loud, every single number.

We know how fast a person really counts, because a man did it, live on the internet, through most of his waking hours, all the way to a million. It took him most of a summer. So the word is easy to say once, and the number is out of reach one by one.

Series: Season 1: Impossible, worked out, part 4 of 6.

Sources
1. 10^9 numbers at one a second is 10^9 s = 31.7 years (Julian years of 365.25 days), said as about 32 years. — mathsisfun.com: https://www.mathsisfun.com/activity/count-billion.html
2. Said in full, numbers grow longer: an average of 13.2 syllables below a million and 20.8 below a billion; one of the longest, 777,777,777, has 31 syllables. — Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_numerals
3. Jeremy Harper counted aloud from 1 to 1,000,000 on a live webcast, 18 June to 14 September 2007: 89 days, about 16 hours a day. — Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Harper_(record_holder)
4. 384 years is 5.2 times the world's life expectancy at birth in 2024 (73.3 years). — un.org: https://www.un.org/sustainabledevelopment/blog/2024/07/press-release-wpp2024/
5. 'One billion' is 3 syllables; counting up to it takes centuries (c6, c8), longer than the longest documented human life (122 years). — guinnessworldrecords.com: https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/oldest-person

Narration: synthetic voice (AI). Animation: code-rendered, no stock footage. Every number is checked against the sources.

Possibility Lab: Impossible questions, honest assumptions, real calculations.
